description: Intent i020 (SNAPSHOT=s05, BRANCH=timer-dwork-softirq-lock) complete. FINDING (medium confidence): drivers/scsi/libiscsi.c:1946-1952, quote "spin_lock(&session->frwd_lock);" — struct iscsi_session.frwd_lock is shared between TIMER_SOFTIRQ callbacks and BH-enabled process context with plain spin_lock() at several sites. Timer-softirq side: timer_setup(&conn->transport_timer, iscsi_check_transport_timeouts) -> spin_lock(&session->frwd_lock) at libiscsi.c:2088, and timer_setup(&conn->tmf_timer, iscsi_tmf_timedout) -> plain lock at 1791. Process holder side: iscsi_eh_cmd_timed_out (1948, scsi .eh_timed_out hook running from blk_mq_timeout_work kworker) and iscsi_send_nopout (1051) / iscsi_itt_to_task (1160) from the iscsi_xmitworker kworker, all plain. ~20 sibling sites on the same lock already use spin_lock_bh (771,1346,1374,1424,1475,1651,1815,1842,1887,2153,2222,2291,2331,2354,2382,2411,2454,2494,2917), proving the lock is softirq-shared and the plain sites violate the driver's own discipline — the timer-softirq analogue of the ks7010 seed mechanism (softirq spins forever against a preempted holder that can never resume: soft lockup/RCU stall/iSCSI stall DoS). Concurrency triggers are attacker-influenced (command timeouts + per-connection transport timer), not data. Candidates classified: slip.c:1404 safe (timer cb is softirq side; all process sites _bh; sl_xmit 498 runs BH-disabled), bcm63xx_enet.c:290 safe (both rx_lock sites softirq-side, no process plain holder), tun.c:490 safe (timer cb softirq side; process sites _bh), cxgb4/sge.c:4025 unresolved (ptp_lock caller contexts untraced), hostap_ap.c:218 unresolved (13 plain vs 24 _bh sites on sta_table_lock; non-timer plain-site contexts untraced). Bounded search: only drivers/ + net/ *.c callbacks registered via timer_setup/setup_timer/DEFINE_TIMER/INIT_DELAYED_WORK/function= were enumerated (73 callback matches triaged); arch/, kernel/, mm/, fs/ and indirectly-wired callbacks not scanned; static analysis only (no .config in tree, no build/lockdep/reproducer), process-context eh_timed_out chain rests on standard kernel wiring; the ks7010 seed itself was not and must not be reported. Artifact: agent-state/findings/i020.json (version 1, snapshots_checked=["s05"], execution_status=complete, 1 finding, 5 candidates, 5 limitations; quote verified to occur literally in the reported 1946-1952 range).
